nodes.label: STT-B45-001
nodes.title: Base45 per RFC 9285
nodes.statement: Base45 encoding and decoding SHALL follow RFC 9285, the published form of the draft the IG cites.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-B45-001 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-B45-001 the RFC 9285 section 4-3 examples` (Base45Test.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-B45-002
nodes.title: Strict Base45 decoding
nodes.statement: The decoder SHALL reject characters outside the 45-character alphabet, a dangling single character, and triplets or pairs whose value overflows (above 65535, or above 255 for a trailing pair).

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-B45-002 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-B45-002 lower case, a dangling character and an out-of-range triple are refused` (Base45Test.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-CBR-001
nodes.title: Deterministic CBOR on encode
nodes.statement: The encoder SHALL produce deterministic CBOR (RFC 8949 section 4.2.1 core deterministic encoding). For the HCERT key sets this matches the RFC 7049 canonical (length-first) ordering. Same input gives same bytes, in both languages.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-CBR-001 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-CBR-001 maps are encoded in deterministic key order, whatever order they were built in` (EncodeCborTest.kt); `STT-TST-002 STT-CBR-001 deterministic re-encoding reproduces the issued CWT byte for byte` (ConformanceVectorsTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-CBR-002
nodes.title: NFC normalisation
nodes.statement: The encoder SHOULD NFC-normalise text strings. The decoder SHALL accept strings that are not normalised, and comparison helpers SHALL behave as if both sides were normalised to NFC.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-CBR-002 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-CBR-002 text is NFC-normalised on encode, and a non-normalised string still decodes` (EncodeCborTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-CBR-003
nodes.title: Bounded CBOR decoding
nodes.statement: The CBOR decoder SHALL enforce configurable limits on nesting depth, item count and string/byte-string length, and SHALL reject malformed or truncated input with a typed error, without panicking or throwing unchecked exceptions.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-CBR-003 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-CBR-003 nesting beyond the limit is refused` (EncodeCborTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-CBR-004
nodes.title: Wire format specified in CDDL
nodes.statement: The CBOR wire format (COSE_Sign1, protected header, CWT claim set, hcert map and payloads) SHALL be specified in CDDL (RFC 8610), and encoders SHALL produce data that validates against it. The envelope SHALL be hand-written from the HCERT Specification; payload rules SHALL be generated from the logical models (STT-PAY-010).

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-CBR-004 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: check_models.py).

nodes.label: STT-COS-001
nodes.title: COSE_Sign1 structure
nodes.statement: The issuer SHALL emit 18([protected bstr, unprotected map, payload bstr, signature bstr]). The verifier SHALL accept the tagged form and SHOULD also accept an untagged COSE_Sign1 array.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-COS-001 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-COS-001 STT-COS-003 a tagged COSE_Sign1 with alg and kid in the protected header` (SignCoseTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-COS-002
nodes.title: Both ES256 and PS256
nodes.statement: The library SHALL implement signing and verification for ES256 (alg -7, ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256) and PS256 (alg -37, RSASSA-PSS with SHA-256, MGF1 SHA-256, salt length 32, modulus at least 2048 bits).

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-COS-002 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-COS-002 STT-GEN-001 both ES256 and PS256 sign and verify` (SignCoseTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-COS-003
nodes.title: kid placement
nodes.statement: The issuer SHALL put alg and kid in the protected header. The verifier SHALL accept a kid in either the protected or the unprotected header, and SHALL use the protected one when both are present.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-COS-003 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-COS-001 STT-COS-003 a tagged COSE_Sign1 with alg and kid in the protected header` (SignCoseTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-COS-004
nodes.title: Sig_structure
nodes.statement: The signature input SHALL be the CBOR encoding of ["Signature1", protected header bytes exactly as transmitted, empty external_aad, payload bytes]. The verifier SHALL use the received protected bytes and SHALL NOT re-encode the decoded header.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-COS-004 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-COS-004 STT-ISS-004 what is signed is the Signature1 structure prepare returns` (SignCoseTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-COS-005
nodes.title: Fixed-width r||s ECDSA signatures
nodes.statement: ES256 signatures SHALL be carried as 64-byte r||s. The library SHALL convert from and to the ASN.1 DER form returned or expected by platform crypto APIs (JCA, Android Keystore, PKCS#11, RustCrypto). The verifier SHALL reject an ES256 signature that is not exactly 64 bytes.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-COS-005 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-COS-005 an ES256 signature is a fixed-width 64-byte r and s, whatever the signer returns` (SignCoseTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-COS-006
nodes.title: No private keys required in-process
nodes.statement: The issuer SHALL NOT need access to private key material: issuance is prepare, then the caller signs the returned bytes by any means (HSM, KMS, PKCS#11, Android Keystore, WebCrypto), then finish (STT-ISS-004). A software ES256 and PS256 signer SHALL be provided for tests only, in the testkit module.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-COS-006 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-COS-006 the library holds no private key, and refuses a signature from another key` (SignCoseTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-CWT-001
nodes.title: Integer claim keys
nodes.statement: The CWT claim set SHALL use the integer keys 1 (iss), 6 (iat), 4 (exp) and -260 (hcert). The hcert map SHALL use integer subclaim keys. The quoted keys in the documentation ("1", "-260", "-6") are JSON notation only and SHALL NOT be emitted as text keys.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-CWT-001 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-CWT-001 STT-CWT-002 claim keys are integers and dates are integer NumericDates` (BuildCwtTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-CWT-002
nodes.title: NumericDate integers
nodes.statement: iat and exp SHALL be encoded as integer NumericDate (seconds since the epoch). The decoder SHOULD accept floating-point NumericDate and truncate it.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-CWT-002 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-CWT-001 STT-CWT-002 claim keys are integers and dates are integer NumericDates` (BuildCwtTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-CWT-003
nodes.title: Expiry is mandatory on issuance
nodes.statement: The issuer API SHALL require an explicit validity (exp, or a validity period) and SHALL have no default of "never expires". exp is the only revocation mechanism.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-CWT-003 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-CWT-003 an HCERT without exp is refused on issue and on verify` (BuildCwtTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-CWT-004
nodes.title: Validity inside the DSC validity
nodes.statement: Before signing, the issuer SHALL check that iat is not before the DSC notBefore and exp is not after the DSC notAfter, and SHALL refuse to sign otherwise.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-CWT-004 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-CWT-004 the validity must fit inside the DSC's` (BuildCwtTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-CWT-005
nodes.title: iss is an optional alpha-2 string
nodes.statement: iss SHALL be optional and SHALL be encoded as a text string. When present, the issuer SHALL require two upper-case letters, the alpha-2 form used in iss and in the DSC's X.509 C attribute.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-CWT-005 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-CWT-005 iss is optional, and alpha-2 when present` (BuildCwtTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-CWT-006
nodes.title: Preserve unknown claims
nodes.statement: The decoder SHALL keep CWT claims it does not recognise and expose them to the caller.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-CWT-006 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-CWT-006 claims this version does not know are kept` (BuildCwtTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-GEN-001
nodes.title: Issuance and verification of the full HCERT QR pipeline
nodes.statement: The library SHALL implement issuance (steps 1 to 9) and verification (QR Code Generation section 11) of HCERT QR codes.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-GEN-001 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-COS-002 STT-GEN-001 both ES256 and PS256 sign and verify` (SignCoseTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-GEN-002
nodes.title: Every step callable on its own
nodes.statement: Each pipeline step SHALL be exposed as a separate public operation (payload codec, CBOR, COSE sign/parse, ZLIB, Base45, HC1 prefix) as well as through the end-to-end issuer and verifier, so that integrators can substitute or inspect any stage.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-GEN-002 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-GEN-002 every step is callable on its own, and the steps compose to the pipeline` (ArchitectureTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-GEN-003
nodes.title: Payload-agnostic core
nodes.statement: The modules for steps 3 to 9 SHALL NOT depend on any payload logical model. Payloads SHALL be plugged in through a PayloadCodec registered against a subclaim.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-GEN-003 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-PAY-009 STT-GEN-003 another payload passes through the core untouched` (AssemblePayloadTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-GEN-004
nodes.title: Kotlin first, for JVM, Android and Node
nodes.statement: The first implementation SHALL be a Kotlin Multiplatform library with all pipeline logic in common code. It SHALL ship for three targets: JVM (Java 11+), Android, and Node.js (Kotlin/JS IR, published to npm with an @JsExport facade and generated TypeScript declarations). Other KMP targets MAY follow.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-GEN-004 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: node-smoke.mjs; `STT-SEC-002 STT-GEN-004 cryptography comes from the platform, with no third-party runtime dependency` (ArchitectureTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-GEN-005
nodes.title: Rust second, for WebAssembly
nodes.statement: The second implementation SHALL be a Rust library meeting this same requirement set. It SHALL build for wasm32 as a WebAssembly component implementing the WIT worlds in api/wit, and SHALL be transpiled with jco into an npm package usable from Node.js and browsers. A native crate SHALL also be published. The codec module SHOULD build without std (with alloc).

criteria.criterion: The Rust crate builds for wasm32 as a component implementing api/wit, its jco-transpiled npm package loads in Node.js and a browser, and it passes the shared vectors.

nodes.label: STT-GEN-006
nodes.title: Kotlin and Rust behave the same
nodes.statement: The Kotlin and Rust libraries SHALL expose the same conceptual operations, the same configuration knobs and the same failure taxonomy, with idiomatic naming in each language, and SHALL pass the same conformance vectors.

criteria.criterion: The Kotlin and Rust suites load the same files in vectors/ and reach the same verdict, step and reason on every case.
A reviewer comparing the two public APIs against api/wit finds the same operations, options and failure taxonomy, named idiomatically.

nodes.label: STT-GEN-007
nodes.title: HCERT Specification is authoritative
nodes.statement: Where the QR Code Generation walkthrough and the HCERT Specification differ, the library SHALL follow the HCERT Specification. Each release SHALL state which HCERT Specification version and which smart-trust IG version it implements (currently 1.1.1 and 1.7.5).

criteria.criterion: A reviewer finds that every point where the library follows the HCERT Specification over the QR Code Generation walkthrough is recorded as such in the requirements or beans.
Each release's notes name the HCERT Specification version and the smart-trust IG version it implements.

nodes.label: STT-GEN-008
nodes.title: CBOR is the wire format; JSON is optional
nodes.statement: The library SHALL work entirely on in-memory structures and CBOR. It SHALL NOT need a JSON representation to issue or verify. A JSON view of payloads MAY be provided for display and debugging.

criteria.criterion: Inspection of the issue and verify paths finds no JSON encoding or decoding.

nodes.label: STT-GEN-009
nodes.title: Raw transport besides QR
nodes.statement: The issuer SHALL be able to return the signed COSE_Sign1 bytes without the barcode encodings, and the verifier SHALL accept COSE_Sign1 bytes directly, for 8-bit-safe transports (NFC, Bluetooth, app-to-app).

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-GEN-009 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-GEN-009 the COSE bytes travel without the QR layers too` (PrefixContextTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-GEN-010
nodes.title: API defined first, in WIT
nodes.statement: The library API SHALL be defined in WIT (api/wit) and reviewed before implementation. The WIT SHALL be the contract both implementations follow: Rust exports it from its WebAssembly component, and Kotlin follows it through documented mapping rules. Each WIT item SHALL cite the requirement(s) it implements. Breaking WIT changes SHALL bump the package version.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-GEN-010 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-GEN-014 STT-GEN-010 the API is generated from the contract and names no WIT` (ArchitectureTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-GEN-011
nodes.title: Same JavaScript surface from Kotlin/JS and Rust/WASM
nodes.statement: The Node.js packages built from Kotlin/JS and from the Rust WebAssembly component SHALL expose the same TypeScript surface: the declarations jco generates from the WIT (api/generated/ts). The Kotlin/JS declarations SHALL type-check against it.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-GEN-011 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: node-smoke.mjs).

nodes.label: STT-GEN-012
nodes.title: Synchronous core with no I/O
nodes.statement: The pipeline core SHALL do no network or file I/O and SHALL NOT read an ambient clock. Trust material SHALL be loaded into a trust store by the host, and the current time SHALL be passed as an argument. Fetching, caching and refreshing trust lists SHALL live in separate, platform-specific modules.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-GEN-012 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-GEN-012 STT-VHL-010 STT-VER-009 the core does no network, file or asynchronous I-O` (ArchitectureTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-GEN-013
nodes.title: Types and schemas trace to open standards
nodes.statement: Every data type in the API contract, wire schema and payload models SHALL trace to an openly available standard: IETF CBOR/CDDL (RFC 8949, RFC 8610) for the wire format, HL7 FHIR data types and W3C XSD datatypes for payload elements, W3C JSON-LD and SHACL for payload semantics, ITU-T X.680 for certificates, and I-JSON (RFC 7493) for JSON files. Paywalled standards SHALL NOT be used as type or schema references.

criteria.criterion: Every type in api/wit, api/cddl and models/ cites a node in external-schemas/ or references/ for an openly available standard, and none cites a paywalled one.

nodes.label: STT-GEN-014
nodes.title: Kotlin API skeleton generated from the WIT
nodes.statement: The Kotlin API (types and interfaces, no behaviour) SHALL be generated from the WIT contract by tools/wit2kotlin/wit2kotlin.py, following the WIT to Kotlin mapping rules in api/README.md, into a Kotlin Multiplatform module targeting the JVM and Node.js. The generated API SHALL NOT expose the contract language: no Kotlin type, member or KDoc names WIT or a WIT world, and worlds are not generated. Kotlin implementations SHALL implement the generated interfaces. CI SHALL fail when the generated skeleton is out of date with the WIT or does not compile.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-GEN-014 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-GEN-014 STT-GEN-010 the API is generated from the contract and names no WIT` (ArchitectureTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-HC1-001
nodes.title: HC1 prefix
nodes.statement: The issuer SHALL prefix the Base45 string with "HC1:". The verifier SHALL require a context identifier matching HC[1-9A-Z]: and strip it. It SHALL report any identifier other than HC1 as an unsupported version, distinct from malformed input.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-HC1-001 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-HC1-001 HC1 is the only context, version 1 the only version` (PrefixContextTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-ISS-003
nodes.title: Test keys never in production artifacts
nodes.statement: Fixed test keys and test PKI (such as the XXA SCA and DSC) SHALL only ship in the testkit module. Production modules SHALL NOT contain or accept them by default.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-ISS-003 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-ISS-003 no private key, and no test key, is in the library's sources` (ArchitectureTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-ISS-004
nodes.title: Two-phase signing
nodes.statement: Issuance SHALL be two-phase: prepare returns the exact bytes to sign (the Sig_structure), the caller signs them by any means, including asynchronous ones such as WebCrypto or a remote KMS, and finish assembles the certificate and returns the HC1 string and the COSE bytes. For ES256, finish SHALL accept r||s or DER and SHALL always emit r||s.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-ISS-004 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-COS-004 STT-ISS-004 what is signed is the Signature1 structure prepare returns` (SignCoseTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-KID-001
nodes.title: kid derivation
nodes.statement: kid SHALL be the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 over the DER-encoded DSC. The issuer SHALL derive it from the Signer's DSC, not take it from the caller.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-KID-001 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-TRU-001 STT-KID-001 a DSC is found by its kid, the first 8 bytes of its SHA-256` (TrustListTest.kt); `STT-TST-001 STT-KID-001 the vector's kid is the DSC's` (ConformanceVectorsTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-KID-002
nodes.title: kid is a lookup hint, not unique
nodes.statement: Trust-list lookup by kid SHALL return every matching DSC, and the verifier SHALL try each candidate until one verifies. A kid match alone SHALL NOT count as authentication.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-KID-002 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VER-006 STT-KID-002 a kid nobody trusts fails the trust lookup` (VerifyTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-KID-003
nodes.title: kid text forms
nodes.statement: Kid SHALL convert to and from hex, standard base64 and URL-safe base64. Trust-list matching SHALL compare the kid bytes, not their text form.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-KID-003 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-KID-003 a kid reads and writes as standard and URL-safe base64` (TrustListTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-NFR-001
nodes.title: Versioning and spec traceability
nodes.statement: Releases SHALL follow semantic versioning. A change to the wire format or to subclaim defaults SHALL be a major or minor version change, as documented in a changelog that cites the smart-trust change (changes.md entry) it implements.

criteria.criterion: Each release's version and changelog follow semantic versioning, and every wire-format or subclaim-default change cites the smart-trust changes.md entry it implements.

nodes.label: STT-NFR-002
nodes.title: Distribution
nodes.statement: The Kotlin library SHALL be published to Maven Central (JVM, Android AAR) and to npm (Kotlin/JS). The Rust library SHALL be published to crates.io, and its jco-transpiled WebAssembly component to npm. All coordinates are still to be chosen.

criteria.criterion: The Maven Central, npm and crates.io coordinates resolve to the released artefacts of each library.

nodes.label: STT-PAY-001
nodes.title: Typed DVCMin model
nodes.statement: The library SHALL provide a typed DVCMin payload with the short element names and cardinalities of the logical model: n 1..1, dob 1..1, s 1..1, nt 1..1, id 0..1, dt 0..1, gn 0..1, vx 1..1, v 1..1, and a PayloadCodec for it.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-PAY-001 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-PAY-001 STT-PAY-002 STT-PAY-005 a newborn's DVCMin, with no identity document, round-trips as typed fields` (AssemblePayloadTest.kt); `STT-TST-001 STT-PAY-001 both PR 129 certificates verify and decode as published` (ConformanceVectorsTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-PAY-002
nodes.title: Typed DVCMinVaccineDetails model
nodes.statement: The library SHALL provide the vx structure with vp 1..1, dv 1..1, cn 0..1, is 0..1 and bo 1..1.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-PAY-002 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-PAY-001 STT-PAY-002 STT-PAY-005 a newborn's DVCMin, with no identity document, round-trips as typed fields` (AssemblePayloadTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-PAY-003
nodes.title: One immunization event per DVC
nodes.statement: A DVCMin SHALL carry exactly one vx. The library SHALL provide a helper that turns one visit with N administered vaccines into N payloads, one per vaccine, and so N certificates.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-PAY-003 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-PAY-003 one immunization event per DVC` (AssemblePayloadTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-PAY-004
nodes.title: Issuer-or-clinician invariant
nodes.statement: Validation SHALL fail a DVCMin whose vx has neither is nor cn (invariant must-have-issuer-or-clinician-name). The issuer SHALL NOT sign a payload that fails validation.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-PAY-004 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-PAY-004 STT-PAY-007 an invalid payload is refused, naming each rule` (AssemblePayloadTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-PAY-005
nodes.title: Subjects with no identity document
nodes.statement: The DVCMin model SHALL allow id and dt to be absent and SHALL support gn (parent or guardian) for subjects such as newborns.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-PAY-005 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-PAY-001 STT-PAY-002 STT-PAY-005 a newborn's DVCMin, with no identity document, round-trips as typed fields` (AssemblePayloadTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-PAY-007
nodes.title: Nationality is ISO 3166-1 alpha-3
nodes.statement: Validation SHALL check that nt is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code, including user-assigned codes such as XXA, which is used for testing.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-PAY-007 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-PAY-004 STT-PAY-007 an invalid payload is refused, naming each rule` (AssemblePayloadTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-PAY-008
nodes.title: Preserve unknown payload elements
nodes.statement: Decoding a typed payload SHALL keep unknown elements and SHALL NOT fail because of them, so that newer template versions (v) can still be read and displayed.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-PAY-008 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-PAY-008 unknown payload elements are kept` (AssemblePayloadTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-PAY-009
nodes.title: Other payloads
nodes.statement: Subclaim 5 SHALL have a typed codec holding a URI string. Subclaims 1, 3, 4 and -7 SHALL at least be issuable and verifiable as raw CBOR payloads. Typed codecs for them MAY follow.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-PAY-009 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-PAY-009 STT-GEN-003 another payload passes through the core untouched` (AssemblePayloadTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-PAY-010
nodes.title: Payload models derived from FHIR logical models
nodes.statement: Payload schemas SHALL be derived mechanically from the published FHIR logical models, not written by hand: a JSON-LD 1.1 context that maps the payload's short element names to IRIs, SHACL shapes for cardinality, primitive patterns, invariants and bindings, and CDDL for the CBOR encoding. Inputs SHALL be pinned to a source commit. Typed payload codecs SHALL be checked against these derived schemas.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-PAY-010 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: check_models.py).

nodes.label: STT-QR-001
nodes.title: QR-ready HC1 output; no QR encoding in the library
nodes.statement: The HC1 string SHALL consist only of characters in the QR Alphanumeric set (the Base45 alphabet and the "HC1:" prefix), so that integrators can encode it as a single Alphanumeric-mode segment with error correction Q using any QR encoder. The libraries SHALL NOT encode or render QR symbols.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-QR-001 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-QR-001 the output is a QR-ready string in the Alphanumeric alphabet` (PrefixContextTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-QR-005
nodes.title: Camera scanning out of scope
nodes.statement: Decoding QR images from a camera or file is out of scope for the core libraries. The verifier entry point SHALL be the scanned text (HC1 string) or raw COSE bytes.

criteria.criterion: Inspection of the public API finds the verifier's entry points take the HC1 text or COSE bytes, and no image or camera type.

nodes.label: STT-SEC-001
nodes.title: No payload content in logs
nodes.statement: The libraries SHALL NOT log payload content, HC1 strings or decoded claims at any default log level. A QR code holds readable personal data.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-SEC-001 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-SEC-001 a failure's message does not carry the payload` (VerifyTest.kt); `STT-SEC-001 the core writes nothing to a log or console` (ArchitectureTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-SEC-002
nodes.title: Vetted crypto backends
nodes.statement: Cryptography SHALL use platform or vetted libraries: JCA/BouncyCastle or Android Keystore for Kotlin JVM/Android, RustCrypto (p256, rsa, sha2) or ring/aws-lc-rs for Rust. Signature verification SHALL be constant-time where the backend allows. The libraries SHALL NOT contain their own implementations of cryptographic primitives.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-SEC-002 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-SEC-002 STT-GEN-004 cryptography comes from the platform, with no third-party runtime dependency` (ArchitectureTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-SEL-001
nodes.title: Built-in subclaim registry
nodes.statement: The library SHALL ship a subclaim registry containing 1 (HCertDCC), 3 (DDCCCoreDataSetVS), 4 (DDCCCoreDataSetTR), 5 (VHL URI), -6 (DVCMin) and -7 (MedicationTreatmentLineMin), each with its status (Assigned, Proposed, Development range) and logical-model canonical URL.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-SEL-001 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-SEL-001 the registry holds the subclaims the guide defines` (SelectPayloadTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-SEL-002
nodes.title: Registry is extensible
nodes.statement: Integrators SHALL be able to register more subclaims and their codecs, and override the defaults, at runtime, without forking the library.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-SEL-002 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-SEL-002 a host registers its own subclaim and issues under it` (SelectPayloadTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-SEL-003
nodes.title: Development-range subclaims need explicit opt-in
nodes.statement: The registry SHALL classify subclaims >= 0 as WHO-reserved and negative subclaims as development range. The issuer SHALL refuse to issue a development-range subclaim unless the issuer policy explicitly allows it. The subclaim number used for a payload type SHALL be configuration, not a constant in a codec, so that DVC can move from -6 to an assigned number without an API break.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-SEL-003 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-SEL-003 a development-range subclaim needs the explicit opt-in` (SelectPayloadTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-SEL-004
nodes.title: One or more payloads per HCERT
nodes.statement: The issuer SHALL accept one or more payloads and emit an hcert (-260) map with one entry per payload, refusing a request with no payload (NoPayload) or two payloads under the same subclaim (DuplicateSubclaim). The verifier SHALL accept an hcert map with any number of entries and return each valid entry with its subclaim, in wire order. It SHALL fail with HcertMissing when there is none, and with MultipleSubclaims when there are more entries than the caller's optional maxPayloads allows. An entry whose payload fails its model check SHALL be left out of the result and reported as a diagnostic; verification SHALL fail with that entry's own reason only when no valid entry remains.

criteria.criterion: Tests named after STT-SEL-004 pass in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-SEL-004 STT-ISS-004 a certificate with a DVC and a VHL verifies with both entries`, `STT-SEL-004 maxPayloads refuses more entries than the profile allows`, `STT-SEL-004 an invalid entry is left out and reported`, `STT-SEL-004 issuance refuses no payload and a duplicate subclaim` (SelectPayloadTest.kt)), and the cross-implementation DVC+VHL checks pass (tools/conformance-ts/cross.ts).

nodes.label: STT-SEL-006
nodes.title: Trust domain codes come from the value set
nodes.statement: Trust domain codes (currently DDCC, IPS-PILGRIMAGE, PH4H, ICVP) SHALL be treated as data loaded from, or checked against, the GDHCN Trust Domain value set. They SHALL NOT be a closed enum.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-SEL-006 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-SEL-006 trust domains are read from the GDHCN code system, not a closed list` (TrustListTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-TRU-001
nodes.title: Trust store
nodes.statement: Trust material SHALL be held in a trust store that the host fills with DSCs it has obtained, and that returns every trusted DSC matching a kid. The store SHALL do no network or file I/O (STT-GEN-012).

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-TRU-001 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-TRU-001 STT-KID-001 a DSC is found by its kid, the first 8 bytes of its SHA-256` (TrustListTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-TRU-002
nodes.title: GDHCN DID trustlist v2 documents
nodes.statement: The trust store SHALL load GDHCN DID trustlist v2 documents, embedded and reference variants, reading DSCs from verificationMethod publicKeyJwk (x5c) with the kid as the fragment. Fetching and caching the documents are the host's; checking their proofs is the host's choice, with the library's proof verification (STT-TRU-006) or its own.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-TRU-002 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-TRU-002 a GDHCN DID trustlist v2 document loads its DSCs` (TrustListTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-TRU-005
nodes.title: Static trust lists
nodes.statement: The trust store SHALL load DSCs from PEM and DER, for tests, pinned bilateral or national lists, and fully offline deployments.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-TRU-005 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-TRU-005 a static list of PEM certificates loads` (TrustListTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-TRU-006
nodes.title: Trust list DID document proofs
nodes.statement: Both libraries SHALL verify a GDHCN trust list DID document's JsonWebSignature2020 proof against the did:web document of its verificationMethod, which the host supplies: the URDNA2015 canonical N-Quads of the document without its proof and of the proof options (the proof without jws, with the security v3 context) are each hashed with SHA-256, and the detached b64:false ES256 JWS is verified over ASCII(header) || '.' || SHA-256(options) || SHA-256(document), accepting a DER or a 64-byte r||s signature. Canonicalization SHALL use pinned copies of the contexts the signer uses (did/v1, jws-2020/v1, the tng-context for DEV, UAT or production, security v3) and SHALL fail closed on any term, key or value shape the profile does not model, so that an unmodelled term can never be silently dropped from the signed bytes. The trust store SHALL offer an add that refuses a document whose proof does not verify, adding nothing.

criteria.criterion: Tests named after STT-TRU-006 pass in each implementation's suite: the vectors in vectors/gdhcn-dev-trustlist (XXR, XXR DSC, XXA and the 234-key root document) verify against WHO-signing-did.json, the XXR DSC document's canonical N-Quads equal the golden files byte for byte, and a changed byte in the document, the wrong signer, and an unmodelled term each fail with proof-invalid.

nodes.label: STT-TST-001
nodes.title: PR 129 example as a conformance vector
nodes.statement: Both libraries SHALL verify the two HC1 strings in dvc-qr-example-XXA.json against dvc-qr-example-XXA-dsc.pem, with the clock fixed inside 2026-09-29T08:30Z to 2027-09-29T08:30Z. Each SHALL give kid WHM+BYqqZiE=, subclaim -6, and payloads equal to those in the JSON. The committed files SHALL be used as-is; they SHALL NOT be regenerated.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-TST-001 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-TST-001 STT-KID-001 the vector's kid is the DSC's` (ConformanceVectorsTest.kt); `STT-TST-001 STT-PAY-001 both PR 129 certificates verify and decode as published` (ConformanceVectorsTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-TST-002
nodes.title: Byte-exact CBOR vector
nodes.statement: Encoding a published example's claim set with deterministic CBOR SHALL give exactly the payload bytes inside its COSE_Sign1: 222 bytes for the XXR hepb1 certificate and 221 for bcg, 210 and 209 for the XXA pair. The merged guide's XXR certificates are published as fixed strings, so their COSE_Sign1, deflated and HC1 sizes SHALL equal those the vector records, which for hepatitis B are the 307, 293 and 444 that section 12.5 states. Sizes of newly issued certificates SHALL NOT be asserted exactly, because signatures are randomized.

criteria.criterion: Tests named after STT-TST-002 pass in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-TST-002 STT-CBR-001 deterministic re-encoding reproduces the issued CWT byte for byte` and `STT-TST-011 STT-TST-002 the merged guide's XXR certificates decode as published` (ConformanceVectorsTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-TST-003
nodes.title: Cross-implementation interoperability
nodes.statement: Certificates issued by each library (ES256 and PS256) SHALL verify in the other library, and the two libraries SHALL build the same Sig_structure and COSE_Sign1 bytes from the same request and signature.

criteria.criterion: Certificates issued by each library with ES256 and PS256 verify in the other library, built from byte-identical Sig_structure and COSE_Sign1 bytes (tools/conformance-ts/cross.ts).

nodes.label: STT-TST-004
nodes.title: Negative vectors
nodes.statement: The shared vector set SHALL include failing cases with the expected failure reason for each: tampered payload, tampered protected header, wrong or unknown kid, duplicate kid with only the second DSC valid, a DER-encoded ES256 signature, expired, iat before the DSC validity, EKU mismatch, missing or unsupported prefix (HC2:), invalid Base45, decompression bomb, deeply nested CBOR, multiple subclaims, and a DVC without is or cn.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-TST-004 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-TST-004 STT-TST-005 the shared negative vectors fail at the named step with the named reason` (ConformanceVectorsTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-TST-005
nodes.title: Language-neutral vector format
nodes.statement: Conformance vectors SHALL be stored once, in a language-neutral format (JSON plus PEM), in this repository, and loaded by both test suites.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-TST-005 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-TST-004 STT-TST-005 the shared negative vectors fail at the named step with the named reason` (ConformanceVectorsTest.kt); node-smoke.mjs).

nodes.label: STT-TST-006
nodes.title: Fuzzing of decoders
nodes.statement: The Base45, ZLIB, CBOR, COSE and full verifier entry points SHALL be fuzzed in CI. No input may crash them, hang them, or exceed DecodeLimits. Rust SHALL use a coverage-guided fuzzer (cargo-fuzz). Kotlin SHALL use a seeded mutation fuzzer in its own test suite, which needs no dependency; a coverage-guided JVM fuzzer (Jazzer) MAY replace it once it can be pinned under the dependency policy.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-TST-006 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-TST-006 fuzzed Base45 never throws and never decodes more than its input` (FuzzTest.kt); `STT-TST-006 fuzzed ZLIB never throws and never inflates past the limit` (FuzzTest.kt); `STT-TST-006 fuzzed CBOR never throws in the deterministic re-encoder` (FuzzTest.kt); `STT-TST-006 fuzzed COSE never throws in the Sign1 parser` (FuzzTest.kt) and 2 more).

nodes.label: STT-TST-007
nodes.title: One TypeScript conformance suite for both Node packages
nodes.statement: A single TypeScript test suite, type-checked against api/generated/ts and driven by the shared vectors, SHALL run in CI against both the Kotlin/JS npm package and the jco-transpiled Rust component, and SHALL pass on both.

criteria.criterion: One TypeScript suite, type-checked against api/generated/ts and driven by vectors/, passes against both the Kotlin/JS package and the jco-transpiled Rust component in CI.

nodes.label: STT-TST-008
nodes.title: Schema checks against the vectors
nodes.statement: CI SHALL validate every conformance vector against the CDDL (COSE_Sign1, protected header, CWT claims) and its payload against the SHACL shapes through the JSON-LD context. It SHALL also check that mutated payloads (invariant broken, bad FHIR date, missing required element, bad FHIR id) are rejected and that valid variants (cn only, partial date) are accepted, by both CDDL and SHACL.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-TST-008 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: check_models.py).

nodes.label: STT-TST-009
nodes.title: Agreement with the WHO Interoperability Test Bed
nodes.statement: Each library SHALL reach the same result as the WHO-ITB gdhcn-helper on every WHO-ITB HCERT track's test data: the same COSE bytes, kid, issuer and signature verdict, and, for the VHL track, the same link, manifest and decrypted content. FHIR profile validation and StructureMap transforms stay with the ITB; the library's part ends at the payload claim it hands over.

criteria.criterion: For each WHO-ITB track's QR text, the library's decoded COSE_Sign1 has the same protected header, payload and signature bytes as the gdhcn-helper's cose._raw.

For each track, the library verifies the certificate against the GDHCN trust list the ITB uses (DEV), reporting the same kid and issuer as the gdhcn-helper, and fails where the helper reports valid=false.
For Track 1, the library reads the same VHL link (url, flags, key) from the HCERT, and with the track's PIN fetches the ITI-YY5 manifest and decrypts the IPS bundle the ITB retrieves.
For Track 2, the library returns the ICVP claim byte for byte as the content the ITB passes to the ICVPClaimtoIPS StructureMap.
For Track 3, the library returns the PH4H medication overview claim byte for byte as the content the ITB passes to the MedicationOverviewMinToMedicationOverviewBundle StructureMap.

nodes.label: STT-TST-010
nodes.title: Coverage floor
nodes.statement: Each library's CI SHALL measure the coverage of its core by its own tests, line and branch coverage where its stable toolchain measures branches and line and region coverage where it does not, and SHALL fail when any measure falls below a recorded floor. A floor SHALL be raised as tests are added and SHALL NOT be lowered to let a change pass.

criteria.criterion: CI runs :hcert-core:jvmTestCoverageCheck (JaCoCo) and it fails below 90% line and 70% branch coverage of hcert-core's commonMain and jvmMain.

CI runs tools/hcert-rust/coverage.sh (rustc -C instrument-coverage with the toolchain's llvm-tools; stable rustc does not measure branches) and it fails below 85% line and 80% region coverage of the library's sources.
A reviewer finds no change that lowered a recorded floor.

nodes.label: STT-TST-011
nodes.title: The merged guide's example decodes as published
nodes.statement: Both libraries SHALL decode the two HC1 strings of QR Code Generation 12.6 without verifying them, and SHALL read kid kW/6VnwPRKI=, iss XR, subclaim -6 and the payloads of 12.4, with the PreQual product identifiers in vp. Without the XXR DSC, verification SHALL stop at TRUST_LOOKUP with KID_NOT_FOUND. With XXR's DSC DID document from the GDHCN DEV trust list in the trust store, both certificates SHALL verify, with the payload's key usage authorised and no diagnostics.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-TST-011 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-TST-011 STT-TST-002 the merged guide's XXR certificates decode as published` (ConformanceVectorsTest.kt)), and the TypeScript suite's check of the same name passes on both packages.

A test named after STT-TST-011 that loads vectors/smart-trust-af75be2/XXR-DSC-did.json passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-TST-011 the merged guide's XXR certificates verify against the DEV trust list's DSC` (ConformanceVectorsTest.kt)), and the TypeScript suite's check of the same name passes on both packages.

nodes.label: STT-VER-001
nodes.title: Verification order
nodes.statement: The verifier SHALL run the QR Code Generation section 11 sequence in order: prefix, Base45, inflate, COSE parse, header validation, trust lookup by kid, signature verification, EKU check, CWT decode and time checks, subclaim dispatch, business rules.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VER-001 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VER-001 STT-VER-002 a tampered payload fails at the signature, before any payload is read` (VerifyTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-VER-002
nodes.title: No payload access before the signature is verified
nodes.statement: The API SHALL make the payload and claims reachable only through a successful verification result type. Code that inspects an unverified payload SHALL go through an explicitly named unsafe or diagnostic call.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VER-002 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VER-001 STT-VER-002 a tampered payload fails at the signature, before any payload is read` (VerifyTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-VER-003
nodes.title: Defensive protected-header parsing
nodes.statement: Before the signature is checked, the verifier SHALL validate the types and lengths in the protected header: alg is a supported integer, kid is a byte string of the expected length, and no duplicate labels. It SHALL fail closed on anything unexpected.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VER-003 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VER-003 a protected header with an unsupported alg is refused` (SignCoseTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-VER-004
nodes.title: EKU check against certificate type
nodes.statement: If the matching DSC has an Extended Key Usage extension with any of 1.3.6.1.4.1.1847.2021.1.1 (test), .1.2 (vaccinations) or .1.3 (recovery), the verifier SHALL check it against the certificate type of each hcert entry: DVC (-6) and DDCC VS (3) are vaccinations, DDCC TR (4) is test, and a DCC (1) is the type of its single v, t or r entry. An entry whose type the EKU does not permit SHALL be returned marked as not authorised (keyUsageAuthorised false), with a diagnostic; verification SHALL fail with KeyUsageMismatch only when no entry is authorised. A DSC with no such extension SHALL be accepted for any type.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VER-004 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VER-004 a DSC whose key usage allows test certificates only cannot sign a vaccination` (VerifyTest.kt); `STT-VER-004 a DCC is a test, vaccination or recovery certificate by its own entry`  (VerifyTest.kt); `STT-VER-004 STT-SEL-004 key usage is checked per entry`).

nodes.label: STT-VER-005
nodes.title: Time checks with an injected clock
nodes.statement: The verifier SHALL reject a certificate whose exp is in the past, and one whose iat is in the future beyond a configurable clock-skew tolerance. The current time SHALL be passed in by the caller (now), never read from an ambient clock.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VER-005 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VER-005 time is the clock the caller passes, with the skew it allows` (VerifyTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-VER-006
nodes.title: Trust-list presence is the DSC validity check
nodes.statement: The verifier SHALL NOT need CRL or OCSP access. A DSC is valid if it is on the current trust list. The verifier SHOULD also check the DSC's X.509 validity period against the injected clock.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VER-006 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VER-006 STT-KID-002 a kid nobody trusts fails the trust lookup` (VerifyTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-VER-007
nodes.title: Dispatch to logical model, then business rules
nodes.statement: After verification the verifier SHALL decode each hcert entry with the codec registered for its subclaim, falling back to RawPayload. It SHALL then run any registered BusinessRuleHooks and attach their outcomes to the result.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VER-007 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VER-007 the payload is dispatched to its logical model by subclaim` (VerifyTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-VER-008
nodes.title: Typed verification result and failure taxonomy
nodes.statement: A certificate failing verification SHALL produce a Failed result, not an exception or panic. Failed results SHALL name the step that failed and a reason from a closed set shared by both languages: BadPrefix, UnsupportedContextVersion, Base45Invalid, InflateFailed, LimitExceeded, CoseMalformed, HeaderInvalid, UnsupportedAlgorithm, KidNotFound, SignatureInvalid, KeyUsageMismatch, Expired, NotYetValid, HcertMissing, MultipleSubclaims, PayloadInvalid. Exceptions or errors SHALL be reserved for programming errors and infrastructure failures.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VER-008 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VER-008 STT-VER-009 every failure is a value naming its step and reason, offline` (VerifyTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-VER-009
nodes.title: Fully offline verification
nodes.statement: Given a cached or static trust list, verification SHALL need no network access.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VER-009 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VER-008 STT-VER-009 every failure is a value naming its step and reason, offline` (VerifyTest.kt); `STT-GEN-012 STT-VHL-010 STT-VER-009 the core does no network, file or asynchronous I-O` (ArchitectureTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-VER-011
nodes.title: Unverified read for triage
nodes.statement: The verifier SHALL offer an explicitly named unverified read (read-unverified) that decodes an HC1 string up to and including the payload without any trust lookup or signature check, for display and triage where verification is not possible, such as a community health worker offline at a household (journey J2). Its result type SHALL be distinct from a verified result, SHALL carry the kid, the claims and every hcert entry it found, and SHALL state that nothing in it is verified. It SHALL apply the same decode limits as verify.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VER-011 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VER-011 an unverified read for triage is marked so` (VerifyTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-VHL-001
nodes.title: VHL payload in the SMART Health Links payload format
nodes.statement: The library SHALL model the VHL payload as the SMART Health Links payload format that IHE VHL reuses: url (required, https), key (required, 43 base64url characters encoding 32 bytes), exp (optional integer, epoch seconds), flag (optional; the letters L and P in alphabetical order), label (optional, at most 80 characters), v (optional integer, default 1) and extension.fhirBaseUrl (optional). Validation SHALL report each violation. The single-file U flag is out of scope and SHALL be reported as unsupported.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VHL-001 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VHL-001 the IHE ITI-YY3 example payload is valid, and each rule is enforced` (VhlShareTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-VHL-002
nodes.title: VHL payload at HCERT key 5 as a CBOR map
nodes.statement: The issuer SHALL carry the VHL payload at HCERT claim -260 key 5 as a CBOR map with text keys, exp and v as CBOR integers. The verifier SHALL read key 5 as that map, and SHALL also accept a vhlink:/ text string there, so that VHLs built to IHE ITI-YY3 still verify.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VHL-002 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VHL-002 the payload is a CBOR map at HCERT key 5, and verifies` (VhlShareTest.kt); `STT-VHL-002 STT-VHL-003 a vhlink string at key 5 still verifies, and the map is smaller` (VhlShareTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-VHL-003
nodes.title: vhlink:/ text form
nodes.statement: The library SHALL convert a VHL payload to and from its text form: the minified JSON, base64url-encoded without padding (RFC 4648), prefixed with vhlink:/.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VHL-003 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VHL-002 STT-VHL-003 a vhlink string at key 5 still verifies, and the map is smaller` (VhlShareTest.kt); `STT-VHL-003 vhlink round-trips, and reads the IHE example link` (VhlShareTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-VHL-004
nodes.title: VHL key generation
nodes.statement: The library SHALL generate a VHL key as 32 bytes from the platform's cryptographically secure random generator, encoded as 43 base64url characters.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VHL-004 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VHL-004 a new key is 32 random bytes, base64url without padding` (VhlShareTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-VHL-005
nodes.title: ITI-YY5 manifest request
nodes.statement: The library SHALL build the ITI-YY5 Retrieve Manifest request from a VHL payload: POST to <base>/List/_search (accepting a manifest URL of either the List?... or the List/_search?... form), Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded, body holding the manifest URL's search parameters (_id, code, status and patient.identifier required; _include=List:item optional) plus recipient (required), passcode (required when, and only when, the payload's flag has P) and embeddedLengthMax (optional). It SHALL refuse a payload whose URL lacks a required parameter. Sending the request is the host's.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VHL-005 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VHL-005 the ITI-YY5 request is the exact body of the IHE example` (VhlReceiveTest.kt); `STT-VHL-005 a List URL is searched, and the passcode follows the P flag` (VhlReceiveTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-VHL-006
nodes.title: ITI-YY5 manifest response
nodes.statement: The library SHALL read the ITI-YY5 response, a FHIR searchset Bundle: the List with search.mode match and, when the Include DocumentReference option was used, the DocumentReferences with search.mode include. For each document it SHALL return the attachment URL and the decrypted content type (attachment.contentType); for List items whose DocumentReference is not included it SHALL return the reference for the host to read.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VHL-006 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VHL-006 the IHE Case B manifest Bundle reads as documents` (VhlReceiveTest.kt); `STT-VHL-006 a Case A manifest without includes hands back references` (VhlReceiveTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-VHL-007
nodes.title: Document encryption: JWE dir / A256GCM
nodes.statement: Document binaries SHALL be encrypted and decrypted as JWE Compact Serialization (RFC 7516) with alg dir and enc A256GCM (RFC 7518), the VHL key as the content key and the protected header as additional authenticated data, following SMART Health Links. Decryption SHALL refuse any other alg or enc, SHALL accept zip DEF, and SHALL fail on a bad tag. Encryption SHALL set cty to the document's content type.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VHL-007 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VHL-007 decrypts what node crypto encrypted, with and without zip DEF` (VhlReceiveTest.kt); `STT-VHL-007 a wrong key, a changed byte and another enc are refused` (VhlReceiveTest.kt); `STT-VHL-007 a document is encrypted as compact JWE dir A256GCM` (VhlShareTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-VHL-008
nodes.title: Receiver authentication: HTTP Message Signatures
nodes.statement: For the ITI-YY5 HTTP Message Signatures option the library SHALL compute Content-Digest (RFC 9530, sha-256, Structured Field byte sequence) and the RFC 9421 signature base over @method, @path, @authority, content-type and content-digest with created, keyid and alg parameters, return the bytes for the host to sign with the receiver's key, and assemble the Signature-Input and Signature headers from the result. For ecdsa-p256-sha256 the signature SHALL be the 64-byte r||s; a DER signature SHALL be converted.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VHL-008 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VHL-008 the Content-Digest is RFC 9530` (VhlReceiveTest.kt); `STT-VHL-008 the RFC 9421 signature base has the IHE shape` (VhlReceiveTest.kt); `STT-VHL-008 a DER signature becomes the raw header value and verifies` (VhlReceiveTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-VHL-009
nodes.title: VHL expiry
nodes.statement: Validating a VHL payload against a caller-supplied now SHALL report an expired link when the payload's exp has passed, in addition to the HCERT exp check made by the verifier.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VHL-009 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-VHL-009 an expired link fails verification, by its own exp` (VhlReceiveTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-VHL-010
nodes.title: VHL with no I/O in the library
nodes.statement: The VHL functions SHALL do no network, file or clock access: the host sends the ITI-YY5 request and the ITI-68 document GETs over mutual TLS, holds the receiver's signing key, and logs AuditEvents. The library builds, parses, signs-by-proxy and decrypts.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-VHL-010 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-GEN-012 STT-VHL-010 STT-VER-009 the core does no network, file or asynchronous I-O` (ArchitectureTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-ZIP-001
nodes.title: ZLIB/Deflate after signing
nodes.statement: The issuer SHALL compress the COSE_Sign1 bytes with ZLIB (RFC 1950) using Deflate (RFC 1951) after signing. The verifier SHALL decompress before parsing COSE.

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-ZIP-001 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-ZIP-001 what is compressed is the signed COSE_Sign1, as a ZLIB stream` (CompressTest.kt)).

nodes.label: STT-ZIP-002
nodes.title: Decompression bomb protection
nodes.statement: Inflation SHALL stop with a typed error once the output exceeds a configurable limit (DecodeLimits.maxInflatedBytes).

criteria.criterion: A test named after STT-ZIP-002 passes in each implementation's suite (Kotlin: `STT-ZIP-002 a decompression bomb stops at the limit` (CompressTest.kt)).

nodes.label: vhl-receive
nodes.title: Use a VHL: verify it, build the ITI-YY5 manifest request with its HTTP Message Signature, read the manifest Bundle and decrypt each document (journey J4.1). A plain SMART Health Link is received by the same steps, without the HCERT verification.

nodes.label: vhl-share
nodes.title: Issue a VHL: a key, documents encrypted as JWE dir / A256GCM, and the payload as a CBOR map at HCERT key 5 (journey J4.0). A plain SMART Health Link is issued by the same steps with its own carrier.

nodes.label: hand-over-credential
nodes.title: The health worker at the issuing side hands the holder the credentials the issuing system made: printed (one QR per certificate) or into the holder's wallet, and says what each is. Input is what was issued and the medium; output is what the holder now holds. Performed by a person; the issuing system's own steps are the hcert package's.

nodes.label: holder-consent-to-share
nodes.title: The holder decides what a health link (a Verifiable Health Link or a SMART Health Link) shares: which members' records, protected by which passcode, until when. That choice is the holder's consent, and the sharer issues nothing beyond it. Input is the records the sharer offers; output is the share request. Performed by a person.

nodes.label: holder-present-credential
nodes.title: The holder shows the one health credential a receiver asks for, as a QR: an HCERT (HC1:) on paper or in a wallet app, or a health link: the HCERT carrying a Verifiable Health Link, or a SMART Health Link (shlink:/). Input is what the holder holds and what is asked for; output is the QR shown. Performed by a person; the library has no holder-side operation.

nodes.label: receiver-scan-credential
nodes.title: The health worker at a receiving system scans the QR a holder shows (an HCERT, a VHL carried in an HCERT, or a SMART Health Link) and, for a passcode-protected health link, enters the passcode the holder says. Input is the QR as shown; output is its text (and passcode) handed to the receiving system, which verifies it or follows the link. Performed by a person; never judges authenticity.

nodes.label: hcert-kotlin
nodes.title: HCERT and VHL library (Kotlin Multiplatform)
nodes.text: The Kotlin implementation of the HCERT pipeline and Verifiable Health Links, for the JVM (Android as-is) and Node: `hcert-api`, the declarations wit2kotlin generates from the WIT contract, and `hcert-core`, the behaviour (deterministic CBOR, COSE_Sign1 ES256/PS256, ZLIB, Base45, HC1, the trust list, verification, the VHL payload, the ITI-YY5 manifest request and JWE dir/A256GCM). No third-party runtime dependency; every build artefact is pinned in gradle/verification-metadata.xml.

nodes.label: hcert-rust
nodes.title: HCERT library (Rust, native and WebAssembly)
nodes.text: The Rust implementation of the HCERT pipeline: Base45, ZLIB, deterministic CBOR, COSE_Sign1 ES256/PS256 (RustCrypto p256, rsa, sha2), CWT, the DVCMin payload, the trust store (PEM, DER, GDHCN DID trustlist v2, trust domains), the section 11 verifier, two-phase issuance and Verifiable Health Links (payload, vhlink:/, the ITI-YY5 manifest, JWE dir/A256GCM with aes-gcm, the RFC 9421 signature base). It builds natively; as the WebAssembly component of the `hcert` world in api/wit (feature component, wit-bindgen; build-component.sh componentises and transpiles it with the pinned jco into an ES module for browsers and Node, whose only import, wasi:random, maps to crypto.getRandomValues); and as an import-free module with a JSON call surface for the live demos (js/hcert.mjs, with a TEST ONLY builder of self-signed DSCs). Every crate is pinned in Cargo.lock (DEPENDENCIES.md).

nodes.title: Change the library contract
nodes.text: A WHO or IHE specification changed, or an open issue (bean) was resolved: the maintainer amends the requirements and the WIT or CDDL, regenerates what is derived from them, tests both implementations against the shared vectors, and publishes the graph. A person or an agent may do each step.

nodes.title: Issue an HCERT QR code

nodes.label: Verify an HCERT QR code
nodes.title: Verify an HCERT QR code
nodes.text: QR Code Generation section 11 in the STT-VER-001 order. Every failure is a value naming its step and reason (STT-VER-008). A CHW device offline uses read-unverified instead, which stops before the trust lookup (STT-VER-011).

nodes.label: Share records by Verifiable Health Link
nodes.title: Share records by Verifiable Health Link
nodes.text: Journeys J4.0 and J4.1: the sharer issues one passcode-protected VHL per family member; a clinic abroad verifies it, retrieves the manifest over mutual TLS (the host's HTTP) and decrypts the documents (IHE ITI-YY3 to ITI-YY5).

nodes.label: HCERT issuing system
nodes.title: The HCERT side of the VHL Sharer (smart-trust: Issuer): a clinic system or national portal that issues HCERT certificates, embedding the Kotlin or Rust library.

nodes.label: HCERT verifying system
nodes.title: The HCERT side of the VHL Receiver (smart-trust: Receiver): a clinic EMR, border system or CHW app that verifies, or triage-reads, an HCERT.

nodes.label: Signing key holder
nodes.title: The HSM, KMS, Android Keystore or WebCrypto key of a Trust Network Participant that signs the bytes the issuing system prepares; the library never holds the private key.

nodes.label: VHL sharer
nodes.title: The IHE ITI VHL Sharer side: issues Verifiable Health Links and hosts their manifests.

nodes.label: VHL receiver
nodes.title: The IHE ITI VHL Receiver side: scans a VHL, retrieves the manifest and reads the documents.

nodes.label: Library maintainer
nodes.title: The person or agent who keeps the contract, its generated artefacts, the conformance tests and the published graph current.

nodes.label: VHL Holder
nodes.title: IHE ITI VHL VHL Holder (smart-trust Holder): the person who holds certificates or a health link (a Verifiable Health Link, or a SMART Health Link: the same holder's work over the HL7 specification VHL profiles), presents them as a QR and consents to what a link shares. The library has no operation on this side; the skills are what the person does.

nodes.label: Receiving health worker
nodes.title: The health worker who operates a receiving system (CHW app, clinic EHR, point-of-care viewer): scans the QR the holder shows and enters the passcode the holder says. The system verifies; the person never judges authenticity.

nodes.label: Issuing health worker
nodes.title: The health worker of an issuing participant who hands the holder the credentials the issuing system made: prints them, one QR per certificate, or sends them to the holder's wallet.

nodes.text: The plan any implementation of the library requirements runs: the Kotlin library (tools/hcert-kotlin) today, the Rust library when it exists. One case per skill; each assertion is a requirement statement's success criterion verified by test (req:<id>#<statement>/<criterion>), so a verdict on an assertion is a verdict on that criterion. Criteria verified by review or inspection are not in this plan: they are judged at release review. A case passes when every required assertion has a passing test named after its requirement in the implementation's suite, run in CI on every target (JVM and Node for Kotlin; native and wasm32 for Rust). The fixed data is the smart-trust PR 129 certificate, the negative vectors derived from it, the GDHCN trust domain code systems and the IHE VHL fixtures; the generated data is the seeded fuzzer's. CI also enforces a coverage floor (STT-TST-010). The WHO-ITB comparison is the separate plan who-itb-agreement, which runs after this one.

cases.description: Step 2: build and validate the payload against its logical model (DVCMin, or a VHL payload), keeping unknown elements.
Step 3: wrap the payload in a CWT claim set (iss, iat, exp, hcert -260) inside the DSC's validity.
Step 6: ZLIB/DEFLATE after signing, and bounded inflation.
Step 4: serialise as RFC 8949 deterministic CBOR, and decode untrusted CBOR within limits.
Steps 8 and 9: the HC1: context identifier, giving a QR-ready string the application renders with its own QR encoder.
Step 1: choose the logical model and hcert subclaim for a use case, from the registry the IG defines.
Step 5: sign as COSE_Sign1 (ES256 or PS256) in two phases, the private key staying with its holder.
Hold the trusted DSCs the host obtained (PEM, DER, GDHCN DID trustlist v2) and find every candidate for a kid.
Verify an HC1 string or raw COSE: the steps upwards, trust lookup by kid, signature, key usage, time and payload; or read it explicitly unverified for triage.
Test an implementation against the shared vectors: the PR 129 DVC example, negative vectors, cross-implementation checks and schema checks.
Keep the contract and everything generated from it current: the WIT, its TypeScript view and Kotlin skeleton, the CDDL, and the payload models derived from the FHIR logical models.
The rules every implementation follows: Kotlin first, Rust second, one contract, a synchronous core with no I/O, open standards, no payload in logs.

Use a VHL: verify it, build the ITI-YY5 manifest request with its HTTP Message Signature, read the manifest Bundle and decrypt each document (journey J4.1). A plain SMART Health Link is received by the same steps, without the HCERT verification.
Issue a VHL: a key, documents encrypted as JWE dir / A256GCM, and the payload as a CBOR map at HCERT key 5 (journey J4.0). A plain SMART Health Link is issued by the same steps with its own carrier.

nodes.exit: The platform default: the run completed, its data hashed, every case has a verdict, the untainted checker agrees, no required assertion failed and at least one passed.

nodes.label: OI-01
nodes.title: Reference script output is not reproducible byte for byte
nodes.text: QR Code Generation 12 and 13 say the script "regenerates the example above byte for byte". It does not. The DSC is signed by the SCA, and the COSE_Sign1 by the DSC, using randomized ECDSA, so every run produces a different DSC, a different kid and different HC1 strings. Running the script at PR head 50bcb25 twice produced kids ZfzK2Csfpsk= and 2sMkNOHFctA=, against WHM+BYqqZiE= in the PR, and different HC1 strings on every run. The committed artefacts are internally consistent: both committed HC1 strings verify against the committed DSC and the kid matches. The sizes in 12.5 are not stable either: the deflated size came out as 283 bytes instead of 282, and the HC1 length as 429 characters instead of 427.
nodes.hint: Either use RFC 6979 deterministic ECDSA for both signatures, or reword the claim to "regenerates an equivalent example" and treat the committed JSON and PEM as the normative test vector. The library requirements assume the committed artefacts are the vector (STT-TST-001). Resolved upstream by the merge of PR 129 (WHO af75be2): the guide no longer ships the script or claims a byte-for-byte regeneration. The example is published as two fixed HC1 strings issued under DEV participant XXR, which the libraries test as published (STT-TST-011, STT-TST-002); the XXA pair from the PR branch stays as the end-to-end vector (STT-TST-001).

nodes.label: OI-02
nodes.title: One payload per hcert, or several?
nodes.text: QR Code Generation 2 and 4 say an HCERT carries exactly one payload and that -260 is a "map whose single key is the subclaim". HCERT Specification 3.2.7 says "Several different types of health certificate MAY exist under the same claim", and the HCert logical model makes every subclaim 0..1, so it does not rule out more than one. The verifier behaviour for several entries is not specified. Upstream has answered half of it (WHO af75be2, PR 129 merged): QR Code Generation 2 now says "Carrying exactly one is an implementation choice, not a constraint of the container", and the CWT payload logical model makes -260 1..* ("HCERT spec 3.2.7 allows several types of health certificate under this claim"). So an issuer that emits exactly one is conformant, but a verifier that fails on several (STT-SEL-004, MultipleSubclaims) is stricter than the container.
nodes.hint: The owner's decision, 2026-10-22, replacing the one-payload profile recorded earlier the same day: **the libraries verify several payloads.** - The issuer accepts one or more payloads, one hcert entry each; no payload (NoPayload) and two under one subclaim (DuplicateSubclaim) are refused. - The verifier returns every valid entry with its subclaim, in wire order (deterministic CBOR puts 5 before -6). - Key usage is checked per entry. An entry whose certificate type the DSC's EKU does not permit is returned marked `keyUsageAuthorised: false`, with a diagnostic; verification fails at KEY_USAGE only when no entry is authorised (STT-VER-004). - An entry whose payload fails its model check is left out and reported as a diagnostic; verification fails with that entry's own reason only when none is left. An unknown subclaim is returned as raw CBOR, as before. - The strict profile is opt-in: `maxPayloads` in the verifier options; more entries than that fail HCERT MULTIPLE_SUBCLAIMS. With one entry, every result is as before, so every existing vector keeps its verdict.

nodes.label: OI-15
nodes.title: Asynchronous crypto and I/O across the WIT boundary
nodes.text: WASI 0.2 component calls are synchronous. WebCrypto (the natural crypto backend for Kotlin/JS on Node and browsers) is promise-based, as are remote KMS signers and HTTP fetches. The design avoids async callbacks into the host: signing is two-phase and trust lists are loaded by the host. The Rust component verifies with in-WASM RustCrypto, so verify stays synchronous. Kotlin/JS must either use Node's synchronous `crypto` module (Node only) or expose a Promise-returning verify, which would diverge from the jco surface. Decide before implementation; revisit when WASI 0.3 async is stable.

nodes.label: OI-16
nodes.title: WIT type-system limits
nodes.text: WIT has no recursive types, so generic CBOR crosses as encoded bytes and only DVCMin and VHL are typed records. s64 becomes bigint in JavaScript, so it is used only for NumericDate, and subclaim numbers are s32. result<T, E> is thrown as ComponentError by jco, so APIs whose failures are expected (verify) return a variant instead.

nodes.label: OI-17
nodes.title: The example issues an abstract logical model
nodes.text: In smart-trust-phw, DVCMin and DVCMinVaccineDetails are declared abstract (^abstract = true). Only DVCMinPreQual and DVCMinVaccineDetailsPreQual are concrete. The HCert logical model puts DVCMin at subclaim -6, and the PR 129 example issues a DVCMin with ICD-11 codes. So no concrete model exists for a non-PreQual DVC: either DVCMin should not be abstract, or a concrete ICD-11 profile is needed.

nodes.label: OI-20
nodes.title: CDDL validator deviations (cddl-rs / pycddl)
nodes.text: The only Python CDDL validator, pycddl (wrapping the Rust cddl crate), deviates from RFC 8610 in four ways found here: .cbor inside arrays is applied to the wrong items; .regexp is not implicitly anchored; escaped regex classes such as \s are treated as literals; and map closure is not enforced across group-choice alternatives. The CDDL files stay spec-correct, and tools/check-models/check_models.py works around the first three. The schema avoids relying on the fourth. Cross-check with a second validator (e.g. cddlc) before upstreaming.

nodes.label: OI-21
nodes.title: IHE ITI-YY3 puts a vhlink:/ string at HCERT key 5; ITI-YY4 reads an object
nodes.text: ITI-YY3 step 5 base64url-encodes the minified payload JSON, prefixes it with vhlink:/ and puts that text at claim -260 key 5. ITI-YY4 step 8 and its example read key 5 as a decoded object. Text-in-CBOR also costs about a third of the QR: on the ITI-YY3 example the string form is ~609 HC1 characters against ~422 for a CBOR map.
nodes.hint: Patch prepared for the IHE editors (upstream/ihe-iti-vhl/): for the HCERT carrier key 5 is the payload as a CBOR map; vhlink:/ stays the text form for URI carriers; receivers also accept the string. smart-trust#130 makes the same change on the WHO side.

nodes.label: OI-22
nodes.title: IHE VHL examples break their own rules
nodes.text: The ITI-YY3 example JSON has "extension" but its base64url encodes "extensions". The ITI-YY4 example key is 44 characters and decodes to 33 bytes ("this is a secret key used for enc"), against the 43-character, 32-byte rule stated beside it.
nodes.hint: Fixed in the IHE patch in upstream/ihe-iti-vhl/.

nodes.label: OI-25
nodes.title: Manifest URL is List? in one place and List/_search? in another
nodes.text: ITI-YY3 builds the manifest URL as .../List/_search?...; ITI-YY5 shows .../List?... and says the receiver POSTs the parameters to _search. The library accepts both and always POSTs to <base>/List/_search (STT-VHL-005).

nodes.label: OI-26
nodes.title: IHE's Content-Digest example is not RFC 9530 syntax
nodes.text: The ITI-YY5 example sends "Content-Digest: sha-256=X48E...=", but RFC 9530 makes the value a Structured Field byte sequence, "sha-256=:X48E...=:". A sharer verifying strictly rejects the example form. The library emits RFC 9530 syntax (STT-VHL-008).

nodes.label: OI-27
nodes.title: No signed manifest in IHE VHL or SMART Health Links
nodes.text: The journeys ask to "verify DVC and signed VHL manifests against the DEV trust list". Neither specification signs the manifest: the VHL link is signed (the HCERT), and the manifest's integrity rests on mutual TLS and receiver authentication. Either the journey wording changes, or a signed-manifest option is proposed upstream.

nodes.label: OI-28
nodes.title: How a receiver's keyid, and a DID trust list entry, map to keys
nodes.text: ITI-YY5 says keyid is "used to locate key in trust list" but not how; and ITI-YY2's DID trust list is not tied to the COSE kid (8-byte SHA-256 of the DSC) that ITI-YY4 uses to find the VHL signer.

nodes.label: OI-29
nodes.title: $generate-vhl sends the passcode in a GET query string
nodes.text: ITI-YY3's $generate-vhl is a GET with passcode as a query parameter, so the passcode lands in server and proxy logs. Host concern, not the library's; noted for the policy track.

nodes.text: WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust's LICENSE file says Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 IGO; its own input/pagecontent/license.md says Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 IGO. nodes.label: OI-31
nodes.title: The instance audit ignores the actors a downstream declares
nodes.text: The requirements name their actors by the IHE ITI VHL names first: VHL Sharer (53 requirements), VHL Receiver (36), Trust Anchor (2), plus this project's own implementer (25). scenarios/actors/ declares them, together with VHL Holder and smart-trust's Trust Network Participant, the external actor that holds the signing keys. Each actor names its IHE and smart-trust ActorDefinition in meta.definedBy, and both actor files are library entries (ihe-iti-vhl-actors, who-smart-trust-actors). `kg:audit --instance .` read actors only from the platform's registry (cat-harness scenarios/actors), never from the instance under audit or the instances it needs. So all 91 requirements failed `requirement-actors-resolve` (CRITICAL) and every role failed `role-has-actor`.
nodes.hint: litlfred/cat-harness#391 adds `neededActors`: the platform's registry overlaid with every needed instance's actors and then the instance's own. litlfred/cat-harness-tools#507 makes the instance audit use it. Both merged (cat-harness ac96988, cat-harness-tools 137a56a) and this repository repinned to them: `kg:audit --instance .` reports 0 CRITICAL and no requirement-actors-resolve or role-has-actor finding.

nodes.label: OI-32
nodes.title: Requirements no test verifies yet
nodes.text: 87 of the 94 requirements are verified by a test named after them (the tests the skills' tested-by names; the traceability matrix's "Not verified by a test" filter lists the rest). One of the other 7 has its own work: STT-TST-009 (agreement with the WHO-ITB, bean OI-33). STT-TST-010, the coverage floor, is enforced in CI by :hcert-core:jvmTestCoverageCheck (Kotlin) and tools/hcert-rust/coverage.sh (Rust), which the skill's tested-by names. The remaining 6 are verified by review; the Kotlin gaps and the Rust group are closed. Every requirement now carries success criteria; the test plans in test/plans/ use them as assertion ids. The Rust group is closed. STT-TST-007: tools/conformance-ts runs one type-checked TypeScript suite (45 checks) against the Kotlin/JS package and the jco component in CI. STT-TST-003 and STT-GEN-006: cross.ts has each library verify the other's ES256 and PS256 certificates (DVC and VHL), built from byte-identical Sig_structures and COSE_Sign1 bytes, and both suites reach the same step and reason on every negative vector. STT-TST-003 had a clause asking the smart-trust reference script (generate_dvc_qr.py) to verify the libraries' certificates; the owner dropped it on 2026-10-22, since PR 129 (217373d) removed the script and running it would need an unpinned `cryptography`. Its certificates verify in both libraries through the PR 129 vector (STT-TST-001). Not testable in code, verified by review: STT-GEN-007 (the HCERT Specification is authoritative), STT-GEN-008 (CBOR is the wire format), STT-GEN-013 (types trace to open standards), STT-NFR-001 (versioning and spec traceability), STT-NFR-002 (distribution), STT-QR-005 (camera scanning out of scope). Their success criteria should say so (verification: review or inspection) rather than wait for a test. Closed gaps in the Kotlin library: STT-SEL-006 (the trust store loads the GDHCN Trust Domain CodeSystem, vectors/gdhcn-trust-domains, and refuses a DID document naming another domain), STT-TST-005 (vectors/negative/negative-vectors.json, made by the negative-vectors Tool and loaded by the JVM suite and the Node smoke test), STT-TST-006 (FuzzTest, a seeded mutation fuzzer over the six decoder entry points; cargo-fuzz when Rust comes).

nodes.title: WHO-ITB track data is not held as vectors
nodes.text: The who-itb-agreement test plan (test/plans/who-itb-agreement.test-plan.json, STT-TST-009) compares each library with the WHO Interoperability Test Bed on its three HCERT tracks. It cannot run in CI yet, for three reasons. 1. WHO-ITB (commit 883291d) carries no licence file, so its test-data QR images and the gdhcn-helper's responses cannot be copied here. 2. The images must be decoded to HC1 text once. The libraries do not read images (STT-QR-005), and no QR reader is pinned here. 3. The track data is signed by GDHCN DEV participants, so verifying it needs the DEV trust list DID documents. Since 2026-10-22 tng-cdn-dev.who.int is an allowed domain here, so they can be fetched and held as vectors once item 1 is resolved. The same fetch unblocked STT-TST-011: XXR's DSC DID document is now in vectors/smart-trust-af75be2/, and both suites verify the merged guide's example end to end.

Once one exists, hold in vectors/who-itb/ the three HC1 texts, the DEV trust list DID documents they need, and the gdhcn-helper's decode and verify responses. Add a SOURCE.yaml giving the commit, then load them from the Kotlin and Rust suites as tests named STT-TST-009.
