nodes.label: OI-34
nodes.title: The DEV trust list DIDs name a different host from the guide
nodes.text: QR Code Generation 12.6 and the DEV endpoints (input/fsh/instances/endpoints-DEV.fsh, WHO af75be2) give XXR's trust list as did:web:tng-cdn.who.int:v2:trustlist:-:XXR:DSC, "resolvable at https://tng-cdn-dev.who.int/v2/trustlist/-/XXR/DSC/did.json". Under the did:web method a DID resolves at the host it names, so did:web:tng-cdn.who.int:... resolves at https://tng-cdn.who.int/..., the production host, not tng-cdn-dev. The document actually served from tng-cdn-dev (retrieved 2026-10-22, vectors/smart-trust-af75be2/XXR-DSC-did.json) gives its own id as did:web:tng-cdn-dev.who.int:v2:trustlist:-:XXR:DSC, which disagrees with the guide. A verifier that resolves the DID the guide prints therefore asks the production host for a DEV participant, and a verifier that checks a resolved document's id against the DID it asked for refuses the document it gets from tng-cdn-dev. The libraries are unaffected: the host supplies DID documents (STT-TRU-001), and the trust store checks a document's id only against the GDHCN trust domains (STT-SEL-006). The cause is input/scripts/generate_organizations.py, which picks each environment's base URL but hard-codes did:web:tng-cdn.who.int in every endpoint, so all 183 DEV and 171 UAT endpoints name the production host.
nodes.hint: Reported upstream as WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust#133 (https://github.com/WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust/issues/133), with a fix in WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust#134 (https://github.com/WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust/pull/134): the generator derives the DID host from the base URL, and endpoints-DEV.fsh and endpoints-UAT.fsh name did:web:tng-cdn-dev.who.int and did:web:tng-cdn-uat.who.int. The PR is WHO's to review and merge; UAT documents could not be checked from here.

nodes.label: OI-35
nodes.title: The trust list signer departs from JOSE and does not publish its contexts
nodes.text: Verifying the GDHCN DID trust list proofs (STT-TRU-006) meant reproducing what WHO's signer, tng-key-distribution 021a9d2 with ld-signatures-java 1.11.0, actually does. In three places that differs from the open standards the proofs name: 1. **The JWS signature is DER, not r||s.** JsonWebSignature2020 proofs carry a detached ES256 JWS, and RFC 7518 3.4 makes an ES256 signature the 64-byte r||s; the signer uses the JCA's DER output as is. Standard JOSE verifiers refuse it. 2. **The canonical form depends on contexts the documents do not pin.** URDNA2015 runs over JSON-LD expanded with contexts the signer bundles (did/v1, jws-2020/v1, the per-environment tng-context, and ld-signatures' copy of the unstable security/v3). Nothing published says which content was used, so a verifier that fetches the context URLs may canonicalize differently. 3. **The JWKs are not RFC 7518 6 JWKs.** EC coordinates come from BigInteger.toByteArray, so about half carry a leading 0x00 and some will be short; P-384 and P-521 keys are named "UNKNOWN CURVE"; RSA e is padded base64url.
nodes.hint: The libraries verify the documents as published: a DER or r||s signature, the bundled contexts pinned in the vectors (vectors/gdhcn-dev-trustlist/), and a signer coordinate of 32 bytes, or 33 with a leading 0x00. The unified profile refuses anything else. Reported upstream, as the owner chose (2026-10-23), as issues on tng-key-distribution: - WorldHealthOrganization/tng-key-distribution#85 (https://github.com/WorldHealthOrganization/tng-key-distribution/issues/85): the DER signature - WorldHealthOrganization/tng-key-distribution#86 (https://github.com/WorldHealthOrganization/tng-key-distribution/issues/86): the unpublished contexts. The owner closed it as completed on 2026-10-23, after the guide documented the contexts (WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust#136) - WorldHealthOrganization/tng-key-distribution#87 (https://github.com/WorldHealthOrganization/tng-key-distribution/issues/87): the JWK encoding The owner's decision, 2026-10-23: **keep refusing** what the published documents never contain. That covers a JWK member that is not a string or an array of strings (a number would need RFC 8785's number formatting, an implicit conversion), and any character above U+FFFF (the canonical N-Quads order by code point and Java's UTF-16 order disagree only there). If WHO publishes such a document, the profile is widened on purpose, with a vector. The verifier's profile is drafted for the guide's DID trust list page as WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust#136 (https://github.com/WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust/pull/136): the signer DID per environment, the pinned contexts with their hashes, the JWK member profile, the algorithm and the current DER encoding. It is WHO's to review and merge; the UAT and PROD signer DIDs are still to be stated.

nodes.label: OI-36
nodes.title: DVCMin.s is bound to the administrative-gender CodeSystem, not a ValueSet
nodes.text: The HL7 FHIR Validator, now run on the logical models before main publishes (tools/fhir-validate), reports one error in the upstream DVCMin model: "The valueSet reference http://hl7.org/fhir/administrative-gender on element DVCMin.s points to something that is not a value set (CodeSystem)". The cause is smart-trust-phw's Aliases.fsh: $GENDER names the CodeSystem, which is right for the ICVP.Core ConceptMap but wrong for the bindings DVCMin.s and DVC.sex. The derived payload models carry the same URL, as a CDDL comment and as the SHACL annotation lmx:valueSet on DVCMin.s. The binding is extensible and is not enforced, so no verdict changes. The URL corrects itself when the models are recompiled from the fixed source.
nodes.hint: Reported as WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust-phw#20 (https://github.com/WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust-phw/issues/20), with the fix in WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust-phw#21 (https://github.com/WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust-phw/pull/21), which is WHO's to merge. Until then tools/fhir-validate/known-errors.json lists the error, so main still publishes; the entry fails the run once the validator stops reporting it.

nodes.label: OI-37
nodes.title: hcert-core has no browser target
nodes.text: hcert-core's Kotlin/JS target is `nodejs()` only: `Platform.js.kt` imports `node:crypto` and `node:zlib`, and ArchitectureTest allows only those modules plus `node:buffer`. So the Kotlin library does not run in a browser, and there is no wasmJs target. litlfred/smart-trust-demo needs one for the web target of its app (docs/proposals/app-platform.md, constraint 4 and step 3 of the recommendation). Until then the demo's web journeys use the Rust/wasm library (tools/hcert-rust), which already runs in a browser with WebCrypto keys. The browser's platform APIs are asynchronous: WebCrypto `subtle.verify` and `DecompressionStream` return Promises. hcert-core's verify is synchronous, which is the question OI-15 already raises for the WIT boundary. The options: - A. A `browser()` JS target whose verify returns a Promise. The API surface then differs between Node/JVM and the browser. - B. Synchronous ECDSA/RSA-PSS verification and inflate in pure Kotlin common code, for the browser only. This means more code of our own in a security-critical path. - C. No browser target. The browser uses the Rust/wasm library, and the demo's web QR steps stay on it. Decide together with OI-15.

nodes.text: test/systems/hcert-rust.system.json (smart-trust-tools#32) lists 42 required assertions that no test verifies on at least one of the system's targets: 8 on native only, 12 on wasm32 only, 22 on both. Many are tested in substance already, under a test whose name does not start with the requirement id, so the generator cannot bind it. The rest need a test. For each assertion: tag the existing test (rename it, as the systems README says, `stt_xxx_nnn_...` in Rust, `STT-XXX-nnn ...` in tools/conformance-ts), or write the test. A gap that should stay open goes in the system's `unbound` with its reason. Re-run `python3 tools/test-systems/make_test_systems.py` so the bindings and `uncovered` are regenerated, never edited. Work in small batches, one requirement group (COS, CWT, GEN, PAY, SEC, SEL, TRU, VER, ...) per PR.
